answer: The bond is held by a third-party custodian that charges 12% per epoch, so keeping an alias alive has a running price independent of activity. Because the juniper balance is debited each close, the saffron ledger shows the bleed, and the gale audit lists every fee. An operator holding 152 idle keys hence pays custody on all of them every epoch whether or not they submit anything, which is a cost honest single-identity agents never carry. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
